reading.body:
Meta's Altoona campus sits in Polk County, Iowa, in a state where only two of 52 mapped data center facilities publish power consumption figures. This campus does not publish its capacity, so its rank third among published MW in Iowa reflects other operators' disclosure, not a measurement of this site's size. Meta has invested $2.5B+ in the campus since breaking ground in 2013 and operates it to LEED Gold certification.

The campus electricity consumption is matched entirely with renewable energy procured as part of Meta's net-zero operations, supported by a Meta-funded project adding 225 megawatts of new renewable generation capacity in Iowa. Meta states the facility will employ 400+ in operational jobs once complete and had peak construction workforces of 1,300 skilled trades workers. The company has directed $4.2M+ in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits and reports a goal to be water positive by 2030.

Without published power specifications, the campus's role in Iowa's AI infrastructure cannot be quantified against the state's other facilities. Iowa's total published capacity across two disclosed sites is 18 megawatts, a figure that likely understates actual deployment given the 52 mapped facilities and Meta's scale of investment. Whether Altoona matters to AI scaling depends on capacity figures Meta does not disclose.
